messages:
sanjay: Heads up — after the terraform bump to the nodepool module (mixed-instance-types + az spread) we're seeing GPUs not coming up in eu-west-3 during scale events. Pods pending with GPU requests, cluster-autoscaler logs show nodegroups created but they never join.

kate: Can you paste the CA logs and the nodegroup create events? Is this the new launchTemplate override we added?

autoscaler-bot: [event] scale_up: requested 3 nodes for deployment/vision-workers (gpu:1). NodeGroup 'gpu-euwest-3' status=Provisioning -> FailedJoin for instance i-0f...

sanjay: here's the relevant snippet from the cloud provider events: `InsufficientInstanceCapacity: We currently do not have sufficient capacity for instance type g4dn.xlarge in eu-west-3a.` Also a few `Failed to attach eni` errors for secondary ENIs.

emily: ENI attach errors usually mean subnet IP exhaustion in that AZ. Did terraform create /26 subnets for the extra AZ? I remember we used /28 during testing in that region.

paul: Confirmed — our terraform var for subnet_sizes in eu-west was accidentally set to small values in the new module defaults. That explains ENI failures and also why instances fail to join.

kate: But why do we still see nodegroups created by ASG/launchTemplate? They spin up but kubelet never registers?

emily: If ENI attach fails the instance boots but can't reach control plane or CNI setup fails so kubelet doesn't join. Also if the launchTemplate uses the wrong IAM policy (we recently tightened it), the node bootstrap can't call STS to get node role tokens.

paul: I grepped the bootstrap logs from a repro instance: `kubelet: failed to get token: access denied`. So two separate issues: subnet IP exhaustion + bootstrap IAM regression.

sanjay: Action plan I'm proposing: 1) revert subnet size var to previous defaults for eu-west in terraform module, 2) roll forward a small IAM patch to add sts:AssumeRole for the node bootstrap role, 3) patch helm values for cluster-autoscaler to enable fallback to alternative instance types and to tune expander to "least-waste" for gpu pools.

kate: For 3) please be explicit — which helm values? We should avoid large rollouts.

emily: Values I tested locally: `--set autoscaler.scaleDownUnneededTime=10m --set autoscaler.expander=least-waste --set autoscaler.balance-similar-nodegroups=true` and for GPU groups `--set nodeGroupSelector.matchLabels.k8s.io/gpu=true` so CA prefers matching nodegroups. Also enable `--set autoscaler.maxNodeProvisionTime=15m` to allow more time for spot fallback.

paul: Note on spot fallback: we saw `InsufficientInstanceCapacity` for g4dn.xlarge in 3a but on-demand g4dn.xlarge was available. We should add a `capacityType` override in terraform for gpu pools to prefer on-demand primary with spot fallback, or at least increase on-demand baseline.

autoscaler-bot: [alert] scaling_policy_violation: gpu-euwest-3 created nodes in a single AZ (3a) violating spread; suggested: `balance-similar-nodegroups` not enabled.

sanjay: Good catch — the new mixed-instance terraform shuffles instance types but we didn't set azDistribution. I'm going to add azAffinity: spread across AZs and ensure `topologySpreadConstraints` are reflected in the launchTemplate tags.

kate: Can someone open a quick PR for terraform with the subnet fix + azDistribution change? I'll handle the helm chart patch and a canary deploy to the eu-west staging cluster. Keep the changes small.

paul: I'll do the tf PR. Plan: revert subnet_sizes variable for eu-west to /24 for the gpu subnets and add an explicit `capacity_type = "ON_DEMAND"` on the default launch template, plus a `spot_pool` fallback list. I'll tag it with `ops:urgent` and include a smoke-test script.

emily: For smoke test, run `kubectl run -i --rm gpu-smoke --image=nvcr.io/nvidia/pytorch:xx --limits=nvidia.com/gpu=1 --requests=cpu=500m` repeatedly until CA scales. Also watch `kubectl get nodes -o wide` to confirm AZ spread.

ops-bot: [runbook] Created incident stub: INFRA-2026-34, linked runbook https://confluence.internal/runbooks/gpu-provisioning. Assigned to @paul and @kate.

sanjay: timeline: tf PR in 30m, helm canary in 45m, smoke tests 60m. If all green we'll roll to prod with short maintenance window.

kate: Also, capture cost impact — switching to more on-demand for gpu pools will increase spend. Please add an estimate to the PR (rough hourly delta). Redwood Finance needs a heads-up if >$2k/day.

paul: Will estimate. My quick calc: 3 extra on-demand g4dn.xlarge ~ $X/hr across region; adding fallback reduces repeated failed spins so it may lower overall cost.

emily: One more check — kube-proxy logs showed `conntrack` high counts in that AZ; if we increase node count we might need to bump conntrack-tuning in the k8s-node helm values to avoid NAT exhaustion. Add that to the canary checklist.

sanjay: Good. I'll update the infra incident and post the runbook link in the PR. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

kate: If we need emergency rollback plan: scale down nodepool replicas via terraform to last known-good count and remove mixed-instance flag. Keep a terraform plan output for quick apply.

paul: PR opened: terraform:fix/eu-west-subnets-176999 — includes tests and smoke script. Linking in 5.

(5 minutes later)

paul: PR link: https://git.internal/r/redwood/infra/compare/terraform:fix/eu-west-subnets-176999 — tests pass in CI except one lint minor.

kate: launching helm canary now to staging with the expander change and maxNodeProvisionTime bump.

autoscaler-bot: [event] scale_up: gpu-euwest-3 staging requested 2 nodes -> provisioning

emily: smoke: pod started, node registered in eu-west-3b, ENI attached OK. Looks promising.

sanjay: Great. Keep watching for ENI attach failures and `FailedJoin` spikes. We'll post a postmortem if anything recurs after prod.
